results.name: City of Arts and Sciences (Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias)
results.why_it_is_special: A futuristic complex designed by Santiago Calatrava featuring an arts centre, IMAX cinema (L'Hemisfèric), Europe's largest aquarium (Oceanogràfic), and a science museum — ultra-modern architecture set amid shallow blue pools and gardens.

results.name: La Lonja de la Seda (The Silk Exchange)
results.why_it_is_special: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996. A masterpiece of late Gothic civic architecture built 1482–1533, with spectacular helical columns, star-shaped ribbed vaults, and the grandiose Sala de Contratación — testimony to Valencia's power as a Mediterranean trading hub.

results.name: Mercado Central (Central Market)
results.why_it_is_special: One of Europe's largest and most impressive indoor fresh-produce markets, celebrated for its grand Art Nouveau architecture with decorative domes and ironwork. A living hub of local food culture and daily life.

results.name: Museo de Bellas Artes de Valencia (Museum of Fine Arts)
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: North of Turia Gardens (San Pio V)
results.why_it_is_special: The second-largest art museum in Spain after the Prado. Housed in a 17th-century building, it holds over 2,000 works spanning the Middle Ages to the 20th century, including masterpieces by El Greco, Goya, Velázquez, and the Valencian painter Joaquín Sorolla.

results.name: IVAM — Institut Valencià d'Art Modern
results.why_it_is_special: The first modern art museum created in Spain (founded 1989). Its collection of over 11,000 works from the 20th and 21st centuries includes paintings, photography, sculpture, video, and comics, with a permanent focus on Julio González. Free entry on Sundays.

results.name: National Museum of Ceramics and Decorative Arts (Marqués de Dos Aguas Palace)
results.why_it_is_special: Housed in the Marqués de Dos Aguas Palace, instantly recognisable by its spectacular Baroque façade. The collection spans ceramic works from the 8th century to the present, reflecting Valencia's historically important ceramics industry.

results.name: Bombas Gens Centre d'Art
results.why_it_is_special: A former industrial workshop transformed in 2014 into a striking contemporary art centre specialising in immersive and audiovisual projects. Spacious, kid-friendly, and architecturally unique.

results.name: Church of San Nicolás de Bari y San Pedro Mártir
results.why_it_is_special: Often called "the Valencian Sistine Chapel" for its breathtaking restored Baroque frescoes covering the entire ceiling and walls — one of the city's most visually stunning hidden treasures.

results.name: Hortensia Herrero Art Center
results.why_it_is_special: A recently opened centre housing over 100 works by major international artists such as Anselm Kiefer, Anish Kapoor, Tony Cragg, and Andreas Gursky, quickly becoming a flagship cultural venue.

results.name: Museo Fallero (Fallas Museum)
results.why_it_is_special: Dedicated to Valencia's most iconic festival, Las Fallas (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage). Displays the *ninots indultats* — the figures saved each year from the bonfires — preserving the artistic and festive heritage of the city.

results.name: Mercado de Colón
results.why_it_is_special: A beautifully restored Art Nouveau market building designed by architect Francisco Mora Berenguer, now functioning as a gourmet food hall and social meeting point — a perfect blend of heritage architecture and modern gastronomy.

results.name: Torres de Serranos
results.why_it_is_special: One of the two surviving fortified medieval city gates and the largest Gothic city gate in Europe — offering panoramic views of the old town and the Turia Gardens from its towers.
